system.summary: Numeric groups of 2-4 digits separated by full stops, set inside clear letters. Most groups split into two numbers of 2-24 (2210 = 22|10, 912 = 9|12); the editors of 1824 printed them as figures because they had no key.
system.notes: Same system in both writers' letters (shared groups 199, 515, 129, 814, 1220), so it is probably Duplessis's cipher with his Paris correspondents in 1593.

prior_solution.where: Brice Dudout, Europe chiffrée (bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#mornay-1593), published Oct 2026 after this project's transcription and failed attempt; key built on P1-P5 and S1, P6 and S2 held out.

conditions.human_role: Asked for a target that needs no archive request; chose this one.

solution.what: Searched the full text of all 12 volumes (archive.org) for chiffre/déchiffré and runs of figures. Mme de Rohan's 1594 letter (vol. 6 LVI) is printed with its decipherment above the figures; Du Maurier and Serviez 1593 (vol. 5), Loménie 24 Feb 1595 (vol. 6 CVII) and Duplessis 1597-98 (vols. 7-8) are printed as bare figures.
Transcribed the eight 1593 passages (93 groups, 62 distinct) from the page images with their clear context (ciphertext.txt).
Split each group into two numbers of 1-24; both halves draw on the same set of values, suggesting each half stands for a letter (a bigram per group).

anneal_pairs.py: number->letter key annealed onto fr-1600-letters (order 4, no spaces) with a French letter-frequency penalty, 10 restarts. No restart produced French; the bigram-per-group reading is not supported at this length.

Built the Mme de Rohan 1594 key (78 values) from the decipherment printed above her figures, vol. 6 pp. 83-85 (rohan1594_key.tsv): letters 6-65, syllables 88-175, word codes 660-919 including 810 = de and 910 = les, and names 10 = le roi, 87 = Paris, 95 = Tours, 96 = Saumur.

Transcribed Loménie to Duplessis, 24 Feb 1595 (15 passages, vol. 6 pp. 179-181), Duplessis to his wife 1595 (vol. 6 p. 182) and Duplessis to Cargroy and to his wife, 18-19 Jan 1597 (11 passages, vol. 7 pp. 124-126) from the page images.

Applied the Rohan 1594 key to the 1595 and 1597 figures. The output does not make French: most groups have no value, and those that do give place names and letters in the middle of words. The key is not the one used in these letters. One partial fit: in Loménie, 'du sieur 810 62 110 4' reads as 'du sieur de ...', so the word-code series ending in 10 may be shared even though the letter values differ.

Brice Dudout (email of 27 Oct 2026, Europe chiffrée) read the 1593 figures: two letters per group, as hypothesis A said, but on a folded alphabet: a = 2, then c-m on rising odd numbers 5-21, n-u on falling even numbers 22-8, 44 = x/y; 1 and 3 never occur, b unattested. His key (key_dudout.tsv) applied to this project's transcription by apply_dudout.py: 93/93 groups give letters; three groups split two ways (219 me/al, 213 an/na, 215 ah/mc) and the sense picks one each time. P1 reads "l'arrest estoit adresse contre le duc de Guise pour le tirer a quatre chevaux", S2 "le roy est trahi". The anneal of step 2 had the right unit but not the key.

Dudout froze the key on P1-P5 and S1 and read P6 and S2 without change (7.6 sd above 2,000 permuted keys, per his page). Our transcription gives the same text letter for letter except P1 'larest' (his 'l'arrest') and S1 'lenteprinse' (his 'l'entreprinse'): either a dropped group in the print or his normalisation; to check on the page image.
Dudout's second email: no group is missing in P1/S1. The cipher gives "larest" and "lenteprinse"; his "l'arrest" and "l'entreprinse" are the normalised spelling of the established text.

Transcribed the remaining bare figures of vols. 7-8 from the archive.org page images (beling/transcription/v7v8_figures.tsv, clear context in a separate file): Mme de Rohan to Mme Duplessis, 27 Feb and 4 Aug 1597 (19 passages, 50 groups), and Duplessis to his wife, Sep 1597-Apr 1598 (15 passages, 79 groups) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Pre-registered test (beling/PREREG.md) of Dudout's folded 1593 key on Lomenie 1595 and Duplessis Jan 1597 (203 groups): coverage 0.655 vs best 0.616 of 200 random number sets (pass needed 0.85, margin 0.30); language score -3.43 per letter, beats 193/200 permuted keys, vs -2.24 on the 1593 control. Inconclusive by the rule; the output makes no words. Shifted keys (c = 1-100) give nothing (Andrew Beling, beling/).
Pre-registered test of the Rohan 1594 key on Mme de Rohan's 1597 figures (50 groups): coverage 0.78, -2.26 per letter, beats 197/200 permuted keys. Fits (small sample) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Rohan 1597 runs read from the 1594 key plus four inferred values (672 = roy, 134 = lo, 38 = g, 160 = ro): 'M. de Villeroy et de Lomenie', 'M. de Cargrois', 'M. de Chastillon' (one sign off), 'le roy'. Two runs not read. Inferred values untested (beling/results/rohan1597_reading.md) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Searched vols. 9-12 for bare figures (OCR of both scans, then page images): Duplessis to his wife Jan-Mar 1599 (30 groups), Mme de Rohan to Duplessis 1599 (4) and Nov 1611-Mar 1612 (84), unsigned letter of 25 Jul 1612 (9); none in vols. 10 and 12. Also the twelve places of the name code 81 63 in vol. 8 (beling/transcription/v9v12_figures.tsv, v8_namecode.tsv) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Pre-registered (beling/PREREG_round2.md): the Rohan 1594 key on Mme de Rohan's 1599 and 1611-12 figures (88 groups): coverage 0.57, -2.69 per letter, beats 85/200 permuted keys; does not fit (another table by 1611). The round-1 inferred values: only 38 recurs (once); extended key beats 130/200 random-value controls; not supported (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Searched for a clear copy of the 1595-99 figures (archive.org, the 1625 edition, web): none. Cribs for Lomenie 24 Feb 1595: the editors' note under the letter (the sieur de Camor's plan against Mercoeur) and the king's same-day cipher letter printed in clear (vol. 6 CVI) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

The cribs make 'du sieur 810 62 110 4' = 'du sieur de Camor' and '810 44 109 27 32 10' = 'de Bretagne' likely; not a key. Lomenie's x10 codes (23/95) are nearly absent from Duplessis's own letters (4/239): probably two systems (beling/results/explore_system.txt, README section 6.5) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Integration check of PR #449: test_folded.py and test_round2.py re-run on the archive.org vol. 6 OCR (sha256 204906c7... matches): T1 folded 1593 key on Lomenie 1595 + Duplessis 1597 coverage 0.655 against best 0.616 (inconclusive; no words), T2 Rohan 1594 key on Rohan 1597 coverage 0.78 and language beats 197/200 (fits, 50 groups), T3 Rohan key on 1599-1612 does not fit, T4 inferred values not supported; all identical. Strictly, only 4 of the 50 Rohan 1597 groups read without an inferred value or a name-code letter; read share recounted 0.182, not 0.247. No second decoder and no image check at the integration check.

gaps.detail: Neither the Rohan 1594 key nor Dudout's folded 1593 key fits (pre-registered, 11 Nov 2026). Cribs from the editors' note and the king's cipher letter CVI of the same day give 'de Camor' and probably 'de Bretagne'; the original of CVI or of Lomenie's letter would give the key.
To his wife and to Cargroy; name codes 81 63, 153 63, 33; few x10 codes, probably not Lomenie's table. Structure only (12 Nov 2026).
1594 key fits; 672, 134, 160 inferred and not seen again; 38 once more (1599), not supported; runs R1 and R18 not read.
Another table; the 1594 key does not fit (pre-registered, 12 Nov 2026).
44 occurs only at the end of P1 and P2; values probable.

outcome.notes: 1593 part read via Dudout's key; 1595-98 open. 11-12 Nov 2026 (Andrew Beling, beling/): vols. 7-12 searched and their figures transcribed (six new documents); the Rohan 1594 key fits Mme de Rohan's 1597 letters but not her 1611-12 ones; Dudout's folded key does not fit 1595-97; the 1595-99 Duplessis/Lomenie figures stay unread. 12 Nov 2026 integration check: all tests re-run and reproduced (corpus hash matches); strict read share 0.182 (contributor's 0.247 counts name-code letters and inferred values); the Rohan 1594 key 'fits' Rohan 1597 on a small sample where only 'le roy' and 'Madame' read without inference.
outcome.method_basis: 1593 Du Maurier/Serviez figures (93 groups) read with the key Brice Dudout published for them (27 Oct 2026), applied to this project's transcription; the 1595-98 figures, a different system, remain not read.

credits.note: Folded-alphabet key for the 1593 figures; held-out check on P6 and S2.

Pre-registered tests of the folded 1593 key (does not fit 1595-97) and of the Rohan 1594 key on Mme de Rohan's 1597 letters (fits) and 1611-12 letters (does not fit); vols. 7-12 figures transcribed; cribs for Lomenie 1595 (beling/).

texts.note: Names and short phrases inside clear letters, so sentences are not expected. The decryption is section T2 of beling/results/mechanical.txt (the Rohan 1594 key unchanged); rohan1597_reading.md proposes M. de Villeroy et de Lomenie, M. de Cargrois, M. de Chastillon and le roy with four inferred values (672 roy, 134 lo, 38 g, 160 ro), untested; runs R1 and R18 not read.

outcome.fraction_read_source: 12 Nov 2026 integration recount, strict (README read bar: guessed, inferred and name-code letter values are holes): 534 code groups in all (1593: 93; Lomenie 1595: 95; Duplessis Jan 1597: 90; Rohan 1597: 50; Duplessis 1597-98: 79; Duplessis 1599: 30; Rohan 1599: 4; Rohan 1611-12: 84; unsigned 1612: 9). Read as sense: the 93 groups of 1593 (Dudout's key) and 4 of the 50 Rohan 1597 groups, the key's own values with no inference (10 = le roy in R10, R13, R15; 11 = Madame in R12); 97/534 = 0.182. The other Rohan 1597 groups that take a value are letters of names that read only with the inferred values 672, 134, 160, 38 (R2, R7, R19), the word-code half of 'le [672]' (R5, R8), or single figures that Beling's own table says are name codes (R3, R4, R6, R11, R14, R16, R17, R18). The contributor's own figure, 0.247 (132/534: every group that takes a value, 39 of the 50 Rohan 1597 groups), is not a read share. Before: 93/278 = 0.335, before vols. 7-12 were transcribed.
